text:
anna: Quick follow-up from the attribution sync. Need to choose a pragmatic architecture for token-level billing + audit. Two broad approaches: 1) attach a tiny fingerprint from the serving path and make downstream joinable, or 2) keep serving path minimal and derive attribution purely in the billing pipeline from request logs. Tradeoffs?
ben: My preference is the tiny fingerprint on every response. If it's fixed-size (10 chars base62) it's cheap and makes downstream reconciliation simple. Avoids heavyweight joins and reduces window for log retention.
carlos: Fingerprint is nice but: 1) it touches the hot path, 2) increases risk if tags leak, 3) requires us to manage a verification key. We should quantify latency/memory impact first.
dee: What about a hybrid: always emit a short fingerprint; have runtime batch small checkpoint blobs periodically (30s) to an append-only ledger. Billing/enrichment joins only need the ledger + events. This keeps hot path tiny and avoids keeping raw logs forever.
anna: Sketching the hybrid: serving runtime writes X-RW-TAG (10 chars) into response header. Billing events include the tag. Runtime nodes also emit compact checkpoint blobs: list of tag->request_id mappings for a time window, signed by node key. Consumers read blobs to reconstruct full provenance. Benefits: fast joins, limited storage, replay-proof.
ben: Ledger blob example (compressed):

{"window_start":1690000000, "window_end":1690000030, "entries":["aZ9kLm3Qp1:req_123","bX1k9N2pQ7:req_124"]}

This is small and compresses well.
carlos: Operational concerns: who stores the ledger? S3-like object store is fine but we need strong durability and indexing by tenant and region. Also need manifest listing to avoid scanning huge buckets.
dee: We can have a manifest per tenant-region per hour that points to minute blobs. Runtime writes blob -> updates manifest (atomic append). Manifest metadata includes region, node id, signed checksum.
anna: Security: tag must not contain PII. Use HMAC(token_seed || tenant_id || short-ts) truncated to base62. Store token_seed in KMS; sign blobs with node key. For audit, we validate HMAC + blob signature.
ben: For cross-region reconciliation, ensure manifest includes region hint and time window. Reconciler can fetch manifests for the tenant for a window and then read the related blobs.
carlos: Sampling: add 1% full traces emitted inline (includes token breakouts) to validate accuracy of enrichment. That helps detect model-mapping regressions and billing drift.
dee: Performance targets proposed: tag generation <0.5ms added latency, ledger write visible within 30s, retention 90d with archival thereafter. Cost estimate: at 2M req/day, 10 bytes/tag -> ~20MB/day pre-compression; manageable.
anna: Decision proposal (for RFC follow-up): 1) adopt hybrid pattern: inline 10-char fingerprint for every response; 2) runtime nodes produce signed, append-only checkpoint blobs every 30s; 3) per-tenant-region manifests index blobs; 4) async enrichment pipeline joins billing events with ledger blobs to produce final tokenized audit records; 5) 1% full-trace sampling and periodic reconciliation jobs.
ben: +1. Action items: runtime change (header + blob producer), blob manifest schema, signer/KMS plan, retention & SLOs, enrichment job design.
carlos: Ping SRE/payments for durability and retention constraints before finalizing retention window. Also add a canary to measure added latency under load.
infra-bot: @anna created pr/eng-platform/5012 (ledger-producer) targeting week 13.
anna: Thanks team, I'll write the RFC follow-up with concrete schemas and cost numbers and loop in payments/sre.
